title: add-neighborhood-perturbation-prober-and-hysteresis-slo-adapter
author: Maya R. Chen
release_notes: Add a neighborhood perturbation prober to detect prompt-set sensitivity and a hysteresis SLO adapter to reduce CI churn; suggests minimal patch candidates when regressions are reproducible.
description:
Context and motivation: We observed intermittent CI failures where small syntactic perturbations to prompts caused outsized quality regressions that were brittle across seeds and model minor-version bumps. This PR introduces a neighborhood perturbation prober that generates controlled, semantically-aware perturbations around each prompt in a prompt-set and a hysteresis-style SLO adapter for CI that uses perturbation stability to decide hard vs soft failures. Goals: 1) Surface regressions that are robust to small semantic-preserving changes (true regressions) vs brittle flakiness, 2) Reduce noisy CI failures by adding a perturbation-stability threshold and a short rolling window (hysteresis) before hard-failing, 3) Produce compact minimal-patch suggestions when degradations are reproducible across perturbation modes.
Summary of changes: - New prober: harness/probers/neighborhood_prober.py implements perturbation modes (duplicate-synonym, punctuation-shift, clause-reorder, paraphasing-proxy) with configurable intensity and a seed-safe stochastic mode. - CI adapter: ci/hooks/hysteresis_slo_adapter.py adds a multi-window decision layer that classifies failures as soft, review-needed, or hard-fail based on perturbation consensus and historical drift budget. - Result reporter: harness/reporters/perturbation_diff_reporter.py produces per-prompt per-mode deltas (precision/recall-style metrics and token-level saliency delta) and exports a compact minimal-patch suggestion when a high-consensus regression is found. - Tests: tests/probers/test_neighborhood_prober.py and tests/ci/test_hysteresis_adapter.py with deterministic fixtures and a small end-to-end smoke test harness/tests/e2e/prompt_neighborhood_smoke.yaml. - Docs: docs/eval/neighborhood-prober.md and a short guidance section in docs/ci/hysteresis-slo.md describing thresholds, recommended defaults, and how to interpret patch suggestions.
Implementation notes: - Perturbation modes are implemented as composable transformers and are intentionally conservative by default; intensity is adjustable per prompt-set via config. - The hysteresis adapter maintains a short in-memory rolling buffer (configurable TTL) of recent soft failures and only escalates to hard-fail when persistent across windows or when perturbation consensus is above the configured threshold. This reduces noisy breakages seen during model rollouts while still surfacing reproducible regressions. - Reporter produces an annotated CSV + JSONL export; the CSV is intended for quick triage, JSONL contains per-example inference traces and token-level saliency diffs for deeper debugging. Backwards compatibility: No test fixtures or existing adapters were removed; default behavior for existing CI pipelines is unchanged unless teams opt into the new adapter via .eval-ci.yaml.
Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for transformer primitives - [x] Integration smoke against a stable local model stub - [x] Documentation for usage and thresholds - [x] Minimal-patch suggester implemented with conservative heuristics - [x] CI checks updated to include adapter when enabled

Review conversation (high-level): Sofia Yang: Nice direction, can we make the default modes opt-in? Response (Maya): defaults are conservative and the adapter is opt-in at the pipeline level; added note in docs.
Carlos Mendez: Strong preference to avoid heavy CPU work in CI; suggest sampling the prompt-set. Response (Maya): implemented per-pipeline sampling rate and added a smokefast mode for quick CI runs.

Eliot Park: Can the minimal-patch suggester output candidate diffs that are human-readable? Response (Maya): reporter emits a compact human-readable CSV with suggested edits and a confidence score; JSONL has machine traces.
Sofia Yang: CI flakey test observed on initial run. Action: re-ran flaky e2e with increased timeout. CI: passed on second run.
